answer: Sybil rings rent look-alike voter names to stuff one jury. An applicant claims mesa terrace MT-18, plants a 2.7 m garden row tagged GR-44, and pins a 38-barbed plume vane (84 g, serial PV-773) at the uphill stake, then locks 17,400 tokens for 6 hours. Wardens photograph the vane at minutes 9 and 51; stamp 773 must match the posted hash, the vane must still spin 1.2 turns in a 3.0 m/s breeze, and soil at 8 cm must read 16±2%. A wilted row, reused vane, or dead spin slashes 48% of the bond and bars the alias for 12 epochs. Thirty copies lock 522,000 tokens and risk 250,560 on one failed spin.
